recipes.name: Cornbread
ingredients: 2 cups (280 grams) cornmeal (Indian Head works best)
1 tablespoon butter, softened at room temperature
instructions: Combine the cornmeal, sugar, kosher salt, egg, vegetable oil, and milk in a bowl and mix well. Let it sit for 20 minutes.
Add the baking powder to the batter and mix well. Brush the butter all over the bottom and sides of an 8 x 8 inch square baking pan.
Insert a toothpick into the center of the bread. It should come out clean. You can bake for a few minutes longer to brown the top.
Remove from the oven. Turn the pan upside down and let the cornbread fall onto your cutting board. Let cool for a few minutes. Cut into bite-size pieces and serve.

ingredient_sections.text: Total time: about 1 hour, including 20 minutes for soaking the cornmeal and 30 minutes for baking.
2 cups (280 grams) cornmeal (Indian Head works best)
1 tablespoon butter, softened at room temperature

instruction_sections.text: Combine the cornmeal, sugar, kosher salt, egg, vegetable oil, and milk in a bowl and mix well. Let it sit for 20 minutes.
Pre-heat the oven 400 degrees F (about 200 degrees C).
Add the baking powder to the batter and mix well. Brush the butter all over the bottom and the sides of baking pan (8 x 8 inch square).
Check to see if it’s fully cooked by inserting a toothpick into the center of the bread. It should come out clean. You can cook a few minutes longer to brown the top of the bread.
Remove from the oven. Turn the pan upside down and let the cornbread fall onto your cutting board. Let cool for a few minutes. Cut into bite size pieces and serve.

I freeze leftover cornbread in individual portions. Wrap each portion in plastic wrap, then place the wrapped portions in a zip-top freezer bag. When you want to eat some, remove the wrapping and reheat it in the microwave directly from frozen, without thawing. The fluffiness and moisture will be revived.
